topic: How do interference mitigation techniques adapt when handling tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic in multi-beam satellite systems?
response: Interference mitigation techniques adapt by optimizing beamforming and power allocation for tunneled traffic, prioritizing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and throughput. For non-tunneled traffic, they focus on minimizing co-channel interference and maximizing spectral efficiency, adhering to standards like ITU-R S.1431 and S.1325.
reference_context: Multibeam satellite systems face interference challenges, addressed by techniques like rate-splitting and beamforming, with standards and recommendations provided by ITU-R for mitigation.
